operations.name: package_test_scripts.md
operations.content:
---
description: p-limit's package.json test script is "xo && ava && tsd"; its tsd file type-checks reject limitFunction on a sync-returning function
---
The inspected `package.json` of the p-limit project at /work/p-limit defines `"test": "xo && ava && tsd"`, so the test command runs the xo linter first and then the ava tests and the tsd type-declaration checks. The tsd file `index.test-d.ts` contains `expectError(limitFunction((_a: string) => 'x', {concurrency: 1}));`, i.e. the tsd type check expects a sync-returning (non-PromiseLike) function to be rejected as `limitFunction` input at the type level. `index.test-d.ts` imports `expectType`/`expectError` from tsd.

In this run's independent verification record the project test command (logged as running `$ xo && ava && tsd`) exited non-zero while the separate behavior and types checks passed: the reported failures were 21 lint errors in the newly added `test-on-idle.js` — mostly `promise/prefer-await-to-then` plus one `@stylistic/arrow-parens` — together with 1 pre-existing non-blocking `no-warning-comments` warning for the TODO comment in `scripts/benchmarker.js`. This records that the lint stage of the same script can fail the test command independently of test results; the failure was left unresolved in the verified source state.

newMemories.name: limiter_on_idle_semantics.md
newMemories.content:
---
name: limiter_on_idle_semantics
description: p-limit onIdle() treats activeCount 0 with an empty queue as idle; reserved slots keep it non-idle
type: project
---
In the p-limit project at /work/p-limit, the added `onIdle()` on the limiter tests idleness as `const isIdle = () => activeCount === 0 && queue.size === 0;`, so a slot already reserved by a queued call counts as busy and keeps `onIdle()` pending until that job finishes.

Waiters are released by `checkIdle()`, which re-reads those live counters on each state change rather than using a cached flag; the added source calls it at the end of `resumeNext()`, at the end of `enqueue()`, in both `clearQueue()` branches, and after the `concurrency` setter's drain loop. Waiters are registered with `idleWaiters.unshift(resolve)` and released with `idleWaiters.pop()()`.

Observed in this run's probes against the modified source: several waiters made while jobs were pending resolved after the job bodies (`a,b,idle1,idle2 0 0`); after `clearQueue()` reported `pending after clear 0 active 1` the waiter was still `result: still pending`; and a job that enqueued another job did not report idle early (`chain result 1`).

Left unresolved here: the probe output labels only the resolution order, so the FIFO release claim rests on the added `unshift`/`pop()` source plus that ordering observation, not on an assertion. The added `index.d.ts` entry `onIdle: () => Promise<void>;` and the widened `limitFunction` result type `& Pick<LimitFunction, 'clearQueue' | 'onIdle'>` are declared type-level contracts read from the declarations, not evidence of runtime enforcement or of a passing test.

newMemories.name: pnpm_test_node20_skip_keep_note.md
newMemories.content:
---
name: pnpm_test_node20_skip_keep_note
description: p-limit's Node-20 test.skip gate is present in test.js and the current Node version does not match it
type: project
---
The existing Memory entry `pnpm_test_node20_skip.md` describes the gate selected for reconsideration in this scope: `const testClearQueueRejects = process.versions.node.startsWith('20.') ? test.skip : test;`. That line is still shown among the `testClearQueueRejects` matches in the grep output collected during this task, and the same snapshot reports `node -v` as `v22.23.2`, so on this run's Node version the `'20.'` prefix condition is not met.

The supplied evidence covers only that conditional selection and the observed Node version; it does not show whether either gated test ran or passed in this run, so no execution outcome is claimed here.
